# Build plan: the redesign, R1–R12

The plan for building the signed-off redesign (git tag `redesign-v9.8.2`) into the live site, one release at a time. Shown to admins at `/admin/development/build-plan`.

## 1. Purpose and how to use this plan

**Source of truth.** The design is the redesign page (`docs/development/redesign.html`, generated by `scripts/redesign/`, shown at `/admin/development/redesign`). Every rule there has a stable id: `AR-nn` for an agreed rule, `AP-nn` for an owner approval inside a rule; open one with [redesign#AR-23](redesign.html#AR-23). This plan names rules by id and a short label only; it never restates them. When this plan and the page disagree, the page wins, and the ledger line wins over a drawing (the page's own rule).

**What the plan fixes.** The order of releases, which release owns each rule (section 7: every AR and AP has exactly one owner), what each release touches in code and data, and the owner decisions (section 2, all decided on 13 October). It does not fix component APIs or copy: that is the per-release spec.

**How to use it.**
1. Before a release: Opus reads its card (section 5), the owned rules on the redesign page and the drawings named, then writes the spec `docs/development/specs/R#.md` (just in time, against the code as it is then). The owner decisions (section 2) are all decided; the spec applies them as written.
2. Sonnet builds from the spec; Opus reviews against the drawings and the owned rules; the reviewer pushes (main deploys); the owner checks on ejam.lumm.eu and tags feedback notes with the release (`R5a: …`).
3. After the release: update its row in section 8 (status, spec link, commits). If a release changes the plan (a rule moves, a release splits), edit this file in the same commit and run `npm run plan:check`.

**Updating.** The plan is living: edit it, never fork it. The specs are the only new files (owner's process of 13 Oct: a just-in-time spec per release); they are frozen once their release is pushed. Rule ids are never renumbered; a new rule on the redesign page gets an owner here before its release is specced (`plan:check` fails until it has one).

**Relation to `docs/execution_handoff.md`.** The handoff keeps one status line per release and a link here; the detail lives here and in the specs. Progress is ticked in both (one line in the handoff, the row in section 8).

**Release names.** The owner's twelve parts keep their numbers. Parts too big for one build and review are split with a letter (R1a, R1b …); each letter is its own release to production.

## 4. Release order

The owner's order stands. Five parts are split into two because each is more than one build and review session (R1, R2, R3, R5, R9: see the sizes in the cards), so there are 17 releases. Two items move:

- **D11 (each group's next meeting) moves from R4 to R3a.** R3a's Informācija gets the "Nākamais pasākums" box (C24), so the query lands with its first user; R5a's card and R6's panel reuse it.
- **The search word chip lands in R5a, the rest of search in R7.** Discovery's search field lives in today's filter bar, which R5a deletes. To avoid a release without search: R2a's header field is a plain form that opens `/?q=…` (works today), and R5a shows the word as the first chip on the filter line ("“sp” ×", part of AR-43). R7 then adds the instant search overlay, the theme chips and the "Atbilst arī:" line.

```
R1a ─► R1b
  └──► R2a ─► R2b ─► R3a ─► R3b
                │      └────────────┐
                │   R4 ─► R5a ─► R5b ─► R6 ─► R7
                │          │      └──────┬─────► R8 (also needs R2a)
                │          └─► R10       └─────► R9a (needs R3a, R4, R6) ─► R9b
                ├─► R11 (any time after R2b)
                └─► R12 (any time after R2b; delete-account needs R2a's Iestatījumi)
```

**Hard dependencies.** R1a before everything (AR-01). R2a needs R1a (tokens). R2b needs R2a (frame for toasts above the bottom bar). R3a needs R2b (counter, pop-ups, skeletons). R3b needs R3a. R4 needs nothing new but must be released before R5a. R5a needs R4 (several cities, counts, event place) and R3a (D11). R5b needs R5a. R6 needs R5b (rows) and R3b (Sazināties). R7 needs R5a (place list, filter line chip) and R6 (results open panels). R8 needs R2a and R5b. R9a needs R3a, R4, R6. R9b needs R9a only for order (shared frame pieces). R10 needs R5a. R11 and R12 need R2b.

**Could run in parallel** (built in separate worktrees, still released one at a time): R4 alongside R3a/R3b (different files except the settings form, which R4 only adds a field to); R11 and R12 alongside anything after R2b; R10 alongside R6–R9. Default: keep the serial order above, because each release is checked by the owner on production.

## 5. Release cards

Common to every card (not repeated): **Acceptance** = Definition of done (AGENTS.md: typecheck, eslint on changed files, `npm run i18n:check`, migration if schema changed) + checked in a running app in lv and en at 375 px and 1280 px, light and dark, side by side with each named drawing, and at 768, 1024, 1440 and 1920 px for the fluid layout (see Cross-cutting: Fluid layout); no horizontal page scroll; Laws respected; `npm run plan:check` passes. **Handbook**: `docs/handbook/design.md` gets its screen entries updated by every release that changes a screen. **UI elements**: every new or changed shared component appears on `/admin/handbook/ui-elements` (`components/handbook/UiElementsDemos.tsx`) with sample data.

### R1a · Identity (M/L)

- **Goal:** today's screens in the new look: Sūna and its neutrals, Literata + Commissioner, the fifteen category tones (light and dark, chosen on the server), soft shapes, small tags, sentence case, dates with the weekday.
- **Rules (owner):** AR-01, AR-03, AR-04, AR-05, AR-06, AR-07, AR-08, AR-09, AR-10, AR-11. Also in: AR-69 (R1b edits what R1a stores).
- **Drawings:** Identity `#h-id` (logo, colour, type, tags, category line, the 15-tone table).
- **Components:** `app/globals.css` (tokens: Sūna, neutrals, danger/success/warning, radii; remove the six `--color-cat-*`; `--primary` keeps its name, used in ~79 files, and takes Sūna instead of indigo), `lib/constants/theme.ts` (Sūna as default preset, with the 15 tones per L1 slug, light and dark), `lib/validations/theme.ts` (theme gains `categories: Record<l1Slug, {light, dark}>`, optional so stored themes still parse), `lib/theme/css.ts` (emits `--cat-<slug>` for `html:root` and `html.dark:root`), `lib/theme-fonts.ts` (preload Literata + Commissioner, stop preloading Geist), `lib/services/taxonomy-resolver.service.ts` + group layout (accent = the L1 tone from the active theme, fallback `Category.color`), `lib/date-format.ts`, `components/ui/{Button,Badge,FilterChip,CategoryIcon}.tsx`, new `components/ui/Logo.tsx` (wordmark + circles), `components/shell/Header.tsx` (logo only; drop the inline `var(--group-accent)` logo colour: the logo is site colour, AR-06), sweep `uppercase` classes (AR-10).
- **Data:** no migration. Builder default from D3: tones live in the site theme (which already has preview and publish); `add_category_color_dark` only if the owner asks for per-category columns. `Category.color` stays as fallback (no contract step).
- **Services/actions:** `ThemeService` (read tones), taxonomy resolver; no new actions.
- **i18n:** `common` (tag words: Eju, Īpašnieks, Mod, Gaida), `theme`.
- **Handbook:** rewrite `docs/handbook/design.md` to the agreed rules (foundations, identity, components, the new page order; remove Geist, indigo, group-colour buttons, layout C) (C31). Voice: sentence case.
- **Risks:** every screen changes at once (visual regressions on 61 screens; the reviewer walks the redesign's [Every live screen](redesign.html#live-screens) list, all 61, at both widths, and the spec lists the routes to open); dark tones must be chosen without client JS (class `.dark` + `html.dark:root` rule, both emitted on the server, Taxonomy Law); L1 slugs in the DB must match the tone keys (check all 15 on the dev DB and prod data).
- **Out of scope:** layout changes, Dizains editing (R1b), header structure (R2a).
- **Acceptance (extra):** contrast: white on every light tone ≥ 4.5:1, near-black on every dark tone ≥ 7:1 (script or test page); no flash of wrong colour on a group page with a cold cache in dark mode; category colour never on a site button (grep `bg-[var(--accent)]` on buttons).
- **Size:** M/L (the token change is small; the sweeps of `uppercase` in ~57 files and of the atoms make it long). The spec measures it as L.
- **Spec:** [specs/R1a.md](specs/R1a.md). Tones are stored per mode in the theme's existing `light` / `dark` JSON (no migration).

### R1b · Admin → Dizains (M)

- **Goal:** Dizains with Krāsas, Kategoriju krāsas and Fonti; preview for yourself, then publish (the deferred Session 15).
- **Rules (owner):** AR-69. Also in: AR-05.
- **Drawings:** Admin "Desktop · Vietne → Dizains → Kategoriju krāsas", "Phone · Dizains → Kategoriju krāsas".
- **Components:** `app/[locale]/admin/design/page.tsx`, `components/admin/design/{DesignEditor,ColorField,ThemeSample,ThemePresetCard,ThemePreviewBar}.tsx`; split DesignEditor (169 lines) into one component per sub-section; new `CategoryColorsEditor` (15 rows, light/dark, live contrast ratio).
- **Data:** none (theme Json).
- **Services/actions:** `ThemeService`, `actions/theme-actions` (validate tones with the theme schema; contrast check in the service).
- **i18n:** `admin.design.*`.
- **Risks:** preview cookie must also swap the category tones on group pages (today it swaps site tokens only).
- **Out of scope:** the Vietne section frame (R11; Dizains stays at `/admin/design` until then).
- **Size:** M.
- **Spec:** [specs/R1b.md](specs/R1b.md). No migration and no change to the stored theme shape (R1a already stores tones per mode); the contrast floor is checked live in the editor and enforced in `ThemeService` (`CONTRAST_TOO_LOW`); parts are sub-tabs on `/admin/design?part=` until R11. The preview already swaps tones on group pages (R1a pipeline); the spec verifies it.

### R2a · Header, menus, bottom bar, footer, own area (L)

- **Goal:** the new header everywhere (desktop and phone), "LV ▾", profile and shield menus, bottom bar, slim footer, the own-area frame and Iestatījumi with Izskats.
- **Rules (owner):** AR-12, AR-13, AR-14, AR-15, AR-16, AR-17, AR-18, AR-19, AR-20, AR-21, AR-60. Also in: AR-41 (header field), AR-61/AR-65 (pages in the frame).
- **Drawings:** Header and navigation (6), "LV ▾" (1), footer and menus (4), "Desktop · Iestatījumi", own-area drawer "Phone · the drawer, opened".
- **Components:** `components/shell/Header.tsx` (rewrite), `UserMenu.tsx` (Mans profils, Manas grupas, Izveidot grupu, Iestatījumi, Iziet; count slot empty until R8), `AdminMenu.tsx` ("Administrēšanas panelis"), `LanguageSwitcher.tsx` → "LV ▾" list built from `LOCALES`, delete `ThemeToggle.tsx`, `MobileNav.tsx` (Atklāt, Grupas, +, Ziņas, Es), `Footer.tsx` (slim; rendered by discovery and reading pages instead of the locale layout), new `components/shell/HeaderSearchField.tsx` (plain GET form to `/?q=`; becomes the search trigger in R7), new own-area layout (route group, e.g. `app/[locale]/(me)/layout.tsx`, holding `profile/page.tsx`, `profile/my-groups`, `profile/edit`, `messages`, new `settings`; `profile/[username]` stays outside; URLs unchanged; check the route-group caveats in `node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/03-api-reference/03-file-conventions/route-groups.md`), new `components/me/{MeSidebar,MeDrawer}.tsx`, new settings page with Izskats (Gaišs, Tumšs, Kā ierīcē).
- **Data:** none. Builder default for D18: next-themes already stores three states (`enableSystem`) without a flash; a cookie only if the spec finds a server need.
- **Services/actions:** `UserService.getOwnProfile` for the frame header (Context Law: the layout fetches, a provider hydrates the own-area context).
- **i18n:** `shell`, `nav`, new `settings` keys under `profile`.
- **Risks:** moving `/messages` and `/profile` under one layout must not change URLs or break `/profile/[username]`; the header at 375 px for admins overflowed by 11 px on the redesign page once (check the real one); feedback and translate modes keep their switches in the shield menu.
- **Out of scope:** the search overlay (R7), Paziņojumi page and bell look (R8), Mans profils content (R9b), the "new" count (R8).
- **Size:** L (one session if the spec is tight; if the spec runs long, the own-area frame and Iestatījumi split off as R2c, released before R2b).
- **Spec:** [specs/R2a.md](specs/R2a.md). No migration; no R2c split (the own area is the last build step). The bottom bar marks the tab you came from on group pages from a session cookie read by the locale layout (no flash on reload) plus a per-group sessionStorage map for back/forward; Iestatījumi is `/settings` in the `(me)` route group; the own menu has four items until R8 adds Paziņojumi.

### R2b · Behaviour pieces (M)

- **Goal:** the shared behaviour every later screen uses: pop-up rule, toasts, empty states, loading shapes, error state, text counter.

## 6. Cross-cutting

- **Fluid layout (owner, 13 Oct).** The drawings are at 375 and 1280 px and are not pixel specs for other widths. Implementations are fluid between and beyond: bars span the full width (brand left, tools right, search growing in the middle), page content sits in one centred container (`max-w-6xl`, or the layout's reading width), no fixed widths copied from a drawing except side columns, dialog sizes and small parts. Each spec's acceptance lists 768, 1024, 1440 and 1920 px next to 375 and 1280, and the reviewer measures the header and the page container there.
- **Tokens and components first.** R1a fixes tokens and atoms; R2b fixes behaviour pieces. Later releases compose them and add to `/admin/handbook/ui-elements`, which is the component library: a builder looks there before making a new piece (Reuse before creating).
- **Taxonomy Law with images and dark tones.** The accent and the banner background are decided on the server: the group layout's `<style>` sets `--accent` for light (`html:root`) and dark (`html.dark:root`) from the theme's tones; the banner image is an image element rendered on the server (never a URL inside the `<style>` block: a user-supplied URL there is a CSS-injection path); no client resolves a colour. Category colour never on site buttons (AR-06).
- **Context Law for frames.** Group frame (R3a), own area (R2a) and admin (R11) layouts fetch their context through services; providers hydrate; client parts read hooks. The client-fetched group sidebar (`GroupSidebarContent` via an action) goes in R3a; `userRole`/accent props in `MemberCard`, `EventRow`, `AnnouncementCard`, `GroupSettingsForm` go when those are replaced (R3a, R5b, R9b).
- **Components over 150 lines** are split when touched: DiscoveryFilterBar 570 (R5a), TagPicker 604 and MemberCard 270, GroupSettingsForm 285 (R9b), EventCreationWizard 517 (R9a), GroupHeader 398 and GroupTabs 301 (R3a), AdminNav 280 (R11), NotificationCenter 238 (R8), DiscoverySidebar 225 (R5a), DateField 222 (R5b/R9a), Modal 172 (R2b), GroupCard 172 (R5a), SlideoverL1View 297 (R11), GroupCreationWizard 262 (R12).
- **Known debt cleared on the way:** five modals in GroupHeader (R3a/R3b); accent prop-drilling and inline styles (R1a Header logo, R3a, R9b); admin `confirm()` (R11); `TagPicker` `as any` (R9b); `c_common_get` naming in `Header.tsx` (R2a). Anything an agent can fix in a few minutes next to the release is fixed, not logged.
- **Migrations (expand → contract).** R4 `add_group_looking_for`, `add_event_city` (expand) → R5a `require_event_city` (contract); R8 `add_user_my_groups_seen_at` (+ maybe `add_notification_group_relation`); R10 `add_city_coordinates`. No drops in R1–R12. Later, outside this plan: `add_report_target_user` (OD-11).
- **Accessibility.** Icon-only buttons carry the visible word as their label (AP-08 "Sazināties"); truncated filter names keep the full name in the label; dialogs trap focus and return it; panels and sheets close on Esc and Back; day strip and calendar days are buttons named with the full date; white text on images keeps 4.5:1 through the shade; touch targets 44 px; motion respects `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- **Performance.** Preload only Literata and Commissioner (R1a); cached count queries with an index on event city and date (R4); panels load their data once (R6); `loading.tsx` shapes so nothing jumps (R2b); no client fetch for anything a layout already has.
- **Feedback.** The owner tags notes with the release (`R3a: …`); the release's reviewer marks them done with `npm run feedback -- done <id> "…"`.

## 8. Process and status

Per release: (1) Opus writes `docs/development/specs/R#.md` from the card, the owned rules and drawings, against current code and the Next.js docs in `node_modules/next/dist/docs/`; applies the owner decisions of section 2 as written. (2) Sonnet builds; Definition of done. (3) Opus reviews side by side with the drawings at 375 and 1280 px, lv and en, light and dark; R4 and every migration get an independent review. (4) The reviewer pushes; the deploy runs migrations while the old app serves. (5) The owner checks on ejam.lumm.eu and tags notes `R#:`; fixes go into the same release's row until it is closed. (6) The row below and the handoff's line are updated.
